Title: The program registers the SYSTEM and not only the WORK
Evidence of omission: Three working instruments measured with paired positive controls appear ZERO times in both canonical task registers and the objective register: marine-nightly/zoomlab (nightly optical render harness with .webm), /api/health/data + data-health-monitor.yml (503-capable readiness poller that already caught a real production outage), useWebGLGuardrail + the Canvas2D renderer pair. Controls: playwright=3 in each register, uptime_probe=1, WebGLMarineLayer=1, WebGLMarineEngine=30 test files.
Why current objectives do not cover it: All 40 objectives and 65 tasks are phrased as work to build/fix/prove. WS-OBJ-701 (canonical register with persistent IDs) governs the register of TASKS. Nothing enumerates what already exists and runs. This is the parent cause of WS-OBJ-503 being certified on the second .webm lane and of WS-CAN-0037 being scoped to build a harness that exists.
Runtime surfaces affected: CI workflows (27), backend readiness endpoints, frontend render fallbacks, runtime override globals
User impact: Indirect but large: a red optical net stood unread while two blank-layer defects reached the owner by eye
Reliability impact: High - an instrument nobody reads is an instrument that cannot catch a regression
Operational impact: High - 18 of 27 workflows were outside the audit program's green census; one red, one never executed
Finish-line relationship: Supporting (it is the cause of several Blocks-Reliable-Baseline items)
Proposed canonical tasks: WS-CAN-0067 (register the optical harness and read its red), WS-CAN-0070 (an instrument inventory the registers cite)
Acceptance criteria: A generated instrument inventory exists (name, what it measures, where its output goes, who reads it, last-read date); every audit's baseline manifest census is generated from it rather than hand-listed; a workflow that is red or has never run cannot be omitted from a green census
Risk of not adding it: A fourth audit re-discovers the same instruments, or worse, builds a third copy of one

Title: Every runtime path that renders forecast data is enumerated and graded
Evidence of omission: MapWebGL.js:1026-1047 and :1070-1088 swap WebGLMarineLayer -> MarineParticleCanvas and WebGLWindLayer -> WindParticleOverlay. Four triggers incl. a PERSISTENT localStorage key with no reset path. MarineParticleCanvas / WindParticleOverlay / useWebGLGuardrail / force_marine_fallback each appear 0 times in the 12.0 register, the 12.1 register, the objective register and every 12.1 artifact; 0 test files reference either renderer (control: WebGLMarineEngine = 30).
Why current objectives do not cover it: WS-OBJ-101 (every activated layer paints) grades layers, not renderers. WS-OBJ-401 (one authority per responsibility) has the right shape but the convergence map's Render plane does not contain the Canvas2D pair, so nothing in that objective points here. WS-CAN-0012 concerns particle invariants between the two WebGL engines, not fallback policy.
Runtime surfaces affected: MarineParticleCanvas (GPUMarineLayer.js), WindParticleOverlay.js, useWebGLGuardrail.js, MapWebGL.js render tree
User impact: A user can be silently switched to a different renderer with no notice and no way back (localStorage route persists)
Scientific impact: Potentially high and UNMEASURED: whether the Canvas2D stack applies the same colour scales, units and land mask as the WebGL stack is unasserted. Under ONE FORECAST COMPOSITION a second renderer drawing different values is the visual analogue of a second forecast path.
Reliability impact: Medium - the guardrail's seven bypasses all reset lowFpsCount, so an interacted-with map is never graded; and it is disabled on localhost, so local A/B runs a different degradation policy than production
Proposed canonical tasks: WS-CAN-0069 (test stack agreement + fallback disclosure + reset path)
Acceptance criteria: A test asserts both stacks produce the same colour scale, units and land mask at a fixed input; a fallback engagement is visible to the user; the persistent localStorage trigger has a documented reset; the guardrail reports not-sampled as a third state rather than folding it into healthy
Risk of not adding it: A production user sees a different field from the tested one, with no signal to anyone

Title: The runtime override surface is inventoried and its state is reportable
Evidence of omission: 261 distinct window.__RAW_*/__OM_* globals in non-test production frontend code across 143 files. 197 have no reference in any test file. 5 appear anywhere in the entire Audit 12.1 output (1.9%). Two change a DISPLAYED FORECAST QUANTITY: marineEngineDecisions.js:113 __RAW_RATING_SPAN_FADE_HI__ (default 9.5) and WebGLMarineEngine.js:1656 __RAW_BLEND_HEIGHT_HI__ (default 1.4). Exactly one NODE_ENV guard exists across frontend/src/components/map/*.js and it gates an error-boundary detail panel.
Why current objectives do not cover it: WS-OBJ-402 governs THREE named dual-path migrations and its acceptance criterion (a dated arm-or-delete decision) is not even meaningful for a numeric tuning lever. WS-CAN-0043/0032 are one flag each. WS-CAN-0052/0053 are BACKEND env flags - different mechanism, different process. SOTA B12 scores MET for kill-switch discipline, which is precisely the habit that produced the 261.
Runtime surfaces affected: All weather/marine render and decision modules; the zoomlab measuring lane (ZL_FLAGS sets these pre-boot)
User impact: Low directly; high for support - a wrong number cannot be reproduced without knowing 261 bits of hidden state
Scientific impact: Medium - two of them move a displayed forecast quantity
Reliability impact: Medium - 197 have no test, so a default can change or a lever stop being read with nothing reddening
Operational impact: High - a flag wrong in the MEASURING lane is worse than in the measured one, and zoomlab takes exactly these globals as ZL_FLAGS
Proposed canonical tasks: WS-CAN-0068 (generated inventory + CI diff + report non-default state in telemetry)
Acceptance criteria: A generated inventory (name -> file:line -> default -> owner -> expiry) that CI regenerates and diffs, so adding a global without an entry fails; one accessor so every read is instrumentable; non-default overrides included in the truth/telemetry payload. NO flag is deleted as part of closure.
Risk of not adding it: Silent drift in a displayed forecast quantity, and permanently irreproducible support incidents

Proposed canonical tasks: WS-CAN-0071 (adopt the mandates as objectives with a measured debt baseline)

Title: The scheduled surf alert does not state the quality; the repaired path is a manual POST nobody calls
Type: Defect repair (NEW TASK under WS-OBJ-201 reopened)
Evidence of omission: backend/scheduler/__init__.py:14,43-45 registers check_surf_alerts_task from scheduler/surf_alerts.py on IntervalTrigger(minutes=15). Live /api/health confirms it: {id: check_surf_alerts, trigger: interval[0:15:00]}. That file sends "Waves are {h}ft - perfect conditions!" (:94) and "Waves are {h}ft - Go get some!" (:111, WEB PUSH). grep -c surf_alert_body|compute_surf_rating|rating_level -> 0 (control: routes/surf_data/alerts.py -> 8). rating/rating_level sit unread in the same current_conditions dict. The guard test_surf_alert_states_the_quality.py:105 opens ONE hard-coded path - the file that is NOT scheduled.
Why current objectives do not cover it: WS-OBJ-201 is CERTIFIED COMPLETE on LV-06, which traced the SERVING chain (nearshore height, quality, surf_height_m write, sim). It never enumerated the NOTIFICATION consumer, which CLAUDE.md's mandate names explicitly. The certificate is sound for what it checked; its scope was too narrow.
Runtime surfaces affected: backend/scheduler/surf_alerts.py, backend/routes/surf_data/alerts.py, frontend service-worker notificationclick, notificationDeepLinks.js
User impact: CRITICAL and LIVE TODAY - a push notification asserts perfection from height alone every 15 minutes on the CURRENT backend. A blown-out 6 ft and a groomed 6 ft produce the identical push. Secondary: the push deep-links to /map?spot= which nothing reads (control: ~20 files elsewhere use useSearchParams).
Scientific impact: Direct violation of the ONE FORECAST COMPOSITION mandate on a surface the mandate names
Reliability impact: Medium - the guard passes, so nothing would catch a regression here either
Dependencies: None - the rating is already computed and already in the dict
Acceptance criteria: scheduler/surf_alerts.py composes both bodies through the shared helper consuming rating/rating_level; the guard DISCOVERS its census rather than hard-coding a path and demonstrably FAILS on the pre-fix tree naming :94; a test drives check_surf_alerts_task itself and shows two equal heights with different ratings producing different bodies; push and in-app deep links agree on a destination that reads its parameter
Risk of not adding it: Users are told conditions are perfect when they are blown out - the exact failure the mandate was written to prevent, on the one deployed surface that is current
